deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a 20th-century archival index or finding-aid card (typed, with handwritten additions) from the Gauss Nachlass at the Göttingen University Library. It lists manuscript shelfmarks connected with Gauss's geodetic work of 1818-1821 (the Hannover/Lüneburg arc measurement and triangulation) and with his 1820 astronomical observations.

Typed entries:
- Cod. Ms. Gauß 8, Bl. 68-72: measurements in Lüneburg, C.F. Gauß, October 1818.
- 84, Bl. 40-41: triangle network in the Duchy of Oldenburg, by Epailly.
- (same item, apparently): calculations around Lüneburg, C.F. Gauß.
- 126/11-12: Gauß to the Kabinettsministerium, 20.3.1821.
- 87c/19: C.F. Gauß, scale ratio 'v = log n'.
- 87d/22: C.F. Gauß, conformal projection.

Handwritten entries:
- 89a/23-24: Gauß, measurements in Göttingen before 1818, and heights.
- Cod. Ms. Gauß 67/25: Gauß, compilation of angles for points around Hannover, 1821.

A ruled table row follows: '22.5 | 116 | Göttingen | 1820 Apr. 17 | UB Göttingen, Cod. Ms. Gauß 61b/22: planet observation'. A second row reads '1820 | Cod. Ms. Gauß 62c/1ff.: objects of observation 1820'.

A long diagonal pencil stroke runs across the upper typed block. It is probably a cancellation or 'done' mark.

The only mathematically suggestive item is the catalogue title 'Vergrößerungsverhältnis v = log n'. It points to a manuscript, not reproduced here, in which Gauss works with the logarithm of the linear scale (magnification) ratio of a conformal map. That is a standard device in his theory of conformal projections (Hannover projection, 1820s). No derivation appears on this card, so there is nothing to reconstruct.

results.what: Catalogue reference to Gauss's use of the logarithm of the conformal scale ratio ('v = log n') and to a manuscript on conformal projection, in the context of the Hannover survey
results.modern_name: Logarithmic scale factor of a conformal map; conformal (Gauss-Krüger / transverse Mercator type) projection
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (conformal mapping, Copenhagen prize essay 1822/1825; Hannover projection, worked out c. 1820s); later Krüger 1912

deep.surprise_reason: This is a modern archival index card listing shelfmarks and titles. It contains no mathematical content. The topics it names (Hannover survey, conformal projection) are well-documented Gauss work.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the leading '126' is struck through and retyped as '126/11-12'. In 'XFGauß' the X is a typed strike-over of 'C', so the intended reading is 'CFGauß an Kab[inetts]ministerium 20.3.1821'.
'2o.3.1821', '8o', '4o-41' use the letter 'o' for the digit 0, typewriter style: read 20.3.1821, 80, 40-41.
The handwritten lines (89a/23-24 ...; Cod Ms Gauß 67/25 ...) and the table rows are later handwritten additions in ink, not typed.

Table row: shelfmark reads 'Cod Ms Gauß 61 b/22: Planetenbeobachtung'. The second row is ditto marks (" ") standing for 'UB Göttingen, Cod Ms Gauß', followed by '62c/1ff. Beobachtungsgegenstände 1820'.
A diagonal pencil stroke across the upper typed block (a cancellation or check mark) is not noted in the machine transcription.
